origin.description: Lorenz curve of the two-parameter Dagum income distribution.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Population shares in the unit interval.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: The two Dagum parameters. The default is c(2, 2).

origin.details: The ordinates come from the regularized incomplete beta of a power of the population share. If the parameter is not admissible, the default c(2, 2) is used and a warning is issued. The function has class theorLc, so it can be drawn with the theoretical-curve plot and lines methods.

translation.description: Lorenz curve of the two-parameter Dagum income distribution.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Population shares in the unit interval, as a scalar or an array.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: The two Dagum parameters. A scalar is inadmissible because the second value is missing. The default is (2, 2).

translation.details: Admissible parameters follow the R transformation and the lower-tail regularized incomplete beta. Any other parameter warns and substitutes the exponents that belong to (2, 2). The result keeps the shape of p.
translation.value: Lorenz ordinates at p, as a NumPy array of the same shape.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from ineq.theor import lc_dagum

p = np.arange(1, 11) / 10
print(lc_dagum(p, parameter=(3.4, 2.6)))
